question: If sin x = (3)/(5) and x in (0, (pi)/(2)) , then find (1+tan x)/(1-tan x)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a right-angled triangle, if sin x = 3/5, the sides form a standard Pythagorean triplet (3, 4, 5).

Thus, Perpendicular = 3, Hypotenuse = 5, and Base = 4.

We know tan x = Perpendicular ÷ Base = 3/4.

Expression = (1 + 3/4) ÷ (1 − 3/4) = (7/4) ÷ (1/4) = 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin x = 3/5

x ∈ (0, π/2), which means x lies in the first quadrant, so all trigonometric ratios are positive.

**Formula Used:**

sin x = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

tan x = Perpendicular / Base

Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base² (Pythagoras Theorem)

 Base (B) = 4
 Perpendicular (P) = 3
 Hypotenuse (H) = 5

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Perpendicular (P) = 3 units and Hypotenuse (H) = 5 units.

⇒ Base (B) = √(H² − P²)

⇒ B = √(5² − 3²) = √(25 − 9) = √16 = 4 units.

⇒ tan x = P / B = 3 / 4

Now, substitute the value of tan x into the given expression:

⇒ (1 + tan x) ÷ (1 − tan x)

⇒ (1 + 3/4) ÷ (1 − 3/4)

⇒ [(4 + 3) / 4] ÷ [(4 − 3) / 4]

⇒ (7 / 4) × (4 / 1)

⇒ 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Quadrant Rule (ASTC)

In the 1st quadrant (0 to π/2), All ratios are positive. In the 2nd quadrant, Sine & Cosec are positive. In the 3rd, Tangent & Cot are positive. In the 4th, Cosine & Sec are positive.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of integers that satisfy a² + b² = c². Standard base triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25). Multiples of these base numbers are also proper triplets.

Basic Trigonometric Ratios

sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse | cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse | tan θ = Perpendicular / Base.
